steps.title: Coat MatTek Dish with Poly‑D‑Lysine
steps.instruction: Dilute the 0.5 mg/mL PDL stock 1:10 in sterile Milli‑Q water to 0.05 mg/mL, add 200 µL to the center of the glass coverslip of a MatTek glass‑bottom dish, spread gently to cover the edges, incubate 2 h at room temperature in a biosafety cabinet, then aspirate and wash three times with 500 µL sterile H₂O for 5 min each wash.

steps.title: Dissect and Dissociate Hippocampal Tissue
steps.instruction: Excise hippocampi from 2–4 P0 Sprague‑Dawley pups, cut each hippocampus into 3–4 pieces with a sterile razor, let papain dissociation solution sit at room temperature for 5 min, transfer tissue pieces to a 15 mL conical tube, remove excess solution, add 1 mL papain dissociation solution (prepared fresh, kept on ice until 5 min before use) for ~6–8 pieces, incubate 30 min at 37 °C water bath with gentle swirl every 5–7 min, remove papain solution, add 1 mL pre‑warmed plating media, triturate gently 3–4 times with a wide‑bore P1000 tip, add 5 mL pre‑warmed plating media, let large pieces settle >1 min, wet a 40 µm cell strainer with 1 mL pre‑warmed plating media and filter the supernatant, repeat filtration for remaining tissue, centrifuge the pooled cell suspension at 100 × g for 8 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL pre‑warmed plating media, gently dislodge pellet, add 4 mL pre‑warmed plating media, determine cell density and viability (use only if viability > 90 %), plate 50 000 cells at the center of each PDL‑coated MatTek dish, add an equal volume of pre‑warmed NbActiv4, rock gently to spread cells, incubate ≥3 h at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C, then add 2 mL pre‑warmed NbActiv4 and return to incubator; replace 1 mL NbActiv4 every 7 days until DIV 10.

steps.title: Transduce Neurons with AAV (Optional)
steps.instruction: Mix 1 × 10¹⁰ genomic copies of rh10‑PX551 (Cas9) and 1 × 10¹⁰ genomic copies of rAAV2‑px552‑sg‑gria1‑HT (donor) in 50 µL pre‑warmed NbActiv4, add the entire volume directly to the culture media, swirl gently, and return the dish to the incubator at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C until use (HaloTag⁺ cells appear as early as DIV 7, typically ready by DIV 10).

steps.title: Nucleofect Neurons with Plasmids (Alternative)
steps.instruction: Pipette 0.5 µg (1 µL of 0.5 µg/µL stock) of PX551 and 0.5 µg of px552‑sg‑gria1‑HT into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, after steps B1‑19 collect 500 000 cells, pellet at 90 × g for 5 min at room temperature, remove media and resuspend in 20 µL complete P3 Nucleofector® solution (18 µL P3 solution + 4 µL Supplement 1) per 500 000 cells, add the cell suspension to the plasmid tube, transfer the mixture to one well of a 96‑well Nucleocuvette® plate, tap to settle without bubbles, run on 4D‑Nucleofector® using program CU‑110, add 80 µL pre‑warmed plating media, recover 5 min at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C, transfer the ~100 µL to 500 µL pre‑warmed plating media, plate 50 000 cells on a PDL‑coated MatTek dish, add an equal volume of pre‑warmed NbActiv4, let adhere ≥3 h at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C, then add 2 mL pre‑warmed NbActiv4 and replace 1 mL NbActiv4 every 7 days until DIV 10.

steps.title: Label HaloTag with Fluorescent Ligand
steps.instruction: At DIV 10 (7 days after AAV infection or 10 days after nucleofection), prepare 20 nM JF 646‑HTL or 10 nM JF 549‑HTL in 2 mL pre‑warmed NbActiv4, aspirate most of the existing NbActiv4 from the dish (leaving a thin layer covering the cells), add the labeling solution, incubate 30 min at 37 °C, then aspirate and wash three times with 2 mL pre‑warmed imaging buffer (total four washes), finally return the dish to the incubator. Perform all steps in a biosafety cabinet using sterile technique and protect dyes from light.

steps.title: Block‑and‑Chase Sparse Labeling
steps.instruction: At DIV 14‑21, prepare 2 mL JF 646‑HTL blocking solution (20 µM JF 646‑HTL + 20 nM cycloheximide in NbActiv4), add to the dish, incubate 1 h at 37 °C, wash three times with pre‑warmed NbActiv4 to remove unbound dye and CHX, incubate 3 h (recovery period; duration may be varied to tune labeling density), prepare 2 mL JF 549‑HTL labeling solution (20 µM JF 549‑HTL in NbActiv4), add to the dish, incubate 30 min at 37 °C, wash three times with 2 mL pre‑warmed imaging buffer, return to incubator for 30 min, then perform a final wash with fresh pre‑warmed imaging buffer.

steps.title: Image Single Particles by HILO Microscopy
steps.instruction: Place the labeled MatTek dish on the microscope stage equipped with an environmental chamber set to 37 °C, locate a healthy GluA1‑HT‑JF 646⁺ neuron using a 640 nm laser (Cy5 channel), switch to 20× then 100× objective as needed, move to a spiny secondary dendrite, adjust Z to the dendrite centre, switch to 561 nm laser (TRITC channel) to view sparsely labeled GluA1‑HT‑JF 549 particles, optimize HILO angle for best signal‑to‑noise, then acquire a timelapse of 400–1000 frames with 20–50 ms exposure per frame (use dual‑camera setup for simultaneous Cy5 and TRITC acquisition if available).

steps.title: Localize Particles with SLIMfast
steps.instruction: Convert the image sequence to TIFF, launch MATLAB, add paths to the image file and SLIMfast folder, run `SLIMfast`, load the TIFF stack, open the OPT dialog and enter acquisition parameters (pixel size 0.16 µm, emission 571 nm, NA 1.49, counts/photon 20.2, lag time 50 ms) and localization parameters (deflation loops 3), close OPT, click LOC ALL to localize all particles, save the localization data, then open the particle data, adjust tracking parameters (maximum expected diffusion coefficient 1 µm²/s, maximum competitors 3, maximum OFF‑time 1 frame) via OPT, and press GEN TRAJ to generate trajectories.

steps.title: Compute Diffusion Coefficients
steps.instruction: In MATLAB run `DiffusionSingle`, open the generated `Image_Sequence.rpt_tracked_table.txt`, outline the region of interest, let the script compute mean‑square‑displacement and diffusion coefficients (lag time 20–50 ms), and export the trajectories and diffusion‑coefficient distribution figures.

steps.title: Curate Tracks Using TrackValidator
steps.instruction: Run `TrackValidator`, load the TIFF image sequence and the corresponding track file (`Image_Sequence.rpt_tracked_table`), inspect each track with the navigation icons, use ‘Delink Track’ to split inaccurate portions, press the Curated icon for correct tracks, then click Save Curated to store a MAT file; move this file into a new folder named “Batch”.

steps.title: Analyze Motion States with HMM‑Bayes
steps.instruction: In MATLAB run `HMM_Batch`, select the Batch folder containing the curated MAT file, and let the program compute motion‑state sequences, probabilities, diffusion parameters, step‑size distributions, and generate figures for each trajectory (lag time can be edited in `HMM_Batch.m`).

steps.title: Identify Vesicles vs Receptors
steps.instruction: From the curated tracks, select those classified as active transport (DV state with high probability). To distinguish single‑receptor from vesicle signals, plot fluorescence intensity over time for several GluA1‑HT‑JF 549 particles, count frames between bleaching steps, take the longest step count, multiply by 4 to set the maximum frames for a homomeric GluA1‑HT (≈100 frames under our conditions); filter out active‑transport trajectories that terminate in fewer frames. For diffusive trajectories, discard particles with diffusion coefficients >0.45 µm²/s or <0.02 µm²/s, as these correspond to surface receptors or tightly trapped clusters respectively.
